title: The gemm task is fp32 and gfx938 declares dot contracts only for fp16 and fp8, so a qualified contraction had no applicable matrix instruction to reach for

evidence.retained: bw1100 /home/testuser01/oci-dcu-runs/gemm-20260917-225918, protocol_adherence adhered, endpoint qualified_by_budget true, best_confirmed_latency_ms 0.409279
sites: the run's candidate artifacts -- lowered_source, ttir, ttgir and amdgcn all contain zero tl.dot, zero mma operations and no v_mmac mnemonic

src/open_cake_ir/tasks/contraction/authoring.py:65 -- the gemm starter, identical in shape on every target: fp32 tensors and a reduce over an elementwise product, with no tl.dot and no instruction contract on any backend, B300 included
compiler/targets/gfx938.json -- dot contracts triton.dot.fp16_fp32 and triton.dot.fp8e4m3_fp32, and no fp32 form
compiler/targets/sm_103a.json -- declares triton.dot.fp32_ieee and triton.dot.fp32_tf32 alongside its reduced-precision forms
measured through Compiler.assess: the gfx938 mma corpus case with its operands moved to fp32 is refused, accepted=False

observation:
An earlier version of this record said the author had the declaration and did not reach for it. That was wrong, and the correction is the finding.

The gemm task is fp32 -- the starter declares fp32 tensors on every target and contracts a reduce over an elementwise product. gfx938 declares dot contracts for fp16 and fp8e4m3 and for nothing else. So no admitted contract covers this workload's dtype, and a contraction written with one would have been refused: the gfx938 mma corpus case with its operands moved to fp32 assesses accepted=False. The author did not decline an available instruction; there was none available for what it was asked to compute.

That the reference bundle names both contracts is what made this look like a choice. It names what the Target declares, not what applies to the case in hand, and the two differ here by dtype alone.

The neighbouring fact is that the starter carries no tl.dot on any target, B300 included, so nothing here shows the DCU behaving differently from the incumbent -- only that the DCU cannot yet be asked to. sm_103a declares triton.dot.fp32_ieee and triton.dot.fp32_tf32; gfx938 declares no fp32 form because none has been measured on it, which is the correct state for an undeclared fact and not a defect.
proposed_change:
Measure fp32 tl.dot on a BW1101 the way the fp16 and fp8 forms were measured -- what the route emits and whether it is correct elementwise against a torch oracle -- and if it holds, declare the contract it earns, with its analyses and a Corpus case in the same change. That is the act F-2026-09-17-008 exists to insist on. Whether the ISA reaches a matrix unit for fp32 operands or falls back to v_fma is part of what the measurement has to say, because a contract that names a matrix instruction the hardware does not run for this dtype would be worse than none.

Until then the fp32 contraction tasks on this target are reduction-shaped by necessity, and that is a coverage limitation to report rather than a result to explain. Do not widen a declared contract to cover fp32 by analogy with the fp16 one: the two are different instructions and the only thing that licenses either is a measurement on the device.
